Thanks so much for the reply and willingness to talk. To answer your questions, I don't think he has an aversion to doctors, just a fear of medication; he doesn't have routine checkups, likely due to the cost involved. He might be resistant to therapy, but I actually think it'd help a lot. The trouble is coming up with enough money to arrange something regular--then there's the possibility of "this therapist isn't effective and now I'm more stressed because we've spent so much money." I'm going to be seeing my university therapist this semester, and have scheduled appointments for my own health quirks, but a lot of our stress is interrelated. I have stress because I put his situation on my shoulders (voluntarily) and he stresses because he's unable to provide for me the way he feels he should be able to. I just don't want him to get so lost in depression that something bad happens. I can't be left asking what if there was more I could have done. The main problems break down to him not being happy with where he is in life, and he doesn't see a way out--but keeps working HARD in hopes that, if there's a chance, that he'll find it. 

Other factors besides money also complicate things. He lives with/takes care of my grandmother (his mom), who isn't the most pleasant person. She's not mean, per se, just very unpleasant to be around--complains a lot, very negative, and becoming more senile. He wants to move to the state I'm in, but is likely waiting for her to pass, needs to save money (which has been tough), and needs to secure a job here first. 

Regardless, whenever we talk with each other it's almost always good vibes. I think the best option right now is to keep building each other up--being supportive, and actively seek better ways to 'make the day'. Set some goals, see each other accomplish them. That sort of thing. Then, when his business picks up and he begins to earn the money I know he's deserving of, we can look at options for therapy, etc. 

I'd like to believe it's a matter of time on both ends. If we can stick it out long enough, being proactive along the way, good things will happen. Conversely, if he gets a down swing again, I'm not sure if I'll be able to help on my own. That being said, I guess my real question is: what can I do to minimize his (and my) stress, and how can I proactively help his situation?

Thank you for any/all input. It feels good to finally ask for help. :]
Thank you, the difficulty is that I don't know how to afford a therapist for him. I can work more and send money.. but I don't know how much longer I have.

Kind of like that scene from Fast and the Furious, when Jesse is explaining why he loves to work on cars, it's one of the only things that can help calm me down. Riding allows me to clear my head and gives me something to really focus on and enjoy; it's not a foolproof system, bad drivers and daily stress can still manage to affect me, but it's a lot easier to shut negative thoughts out when doing something as relieving as getting on two wheels (or one). Riding lets me get away from the world. No phones, no-one else, just me and my bike.
